survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This note reports descriptive results from the OECD Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2024 for lower secondary teachers and principals in Montenegro, using OECD’s TALIS 2024 Database tables. The document does not specify the exact sampling/replicate weight variables or whether complex survey weights were applied in the computations shown. Because the note is a results summary rather than a re-analysis with model-based estimation, the weighting and variance estimation approach is handled upstream in the OECD TALIS database and accompanying tables. Analysts using the underlying TALIS microdata should apply the TALIS sampling weights and replicate design information provided by OECD to obtain population-representative estimates and correct standard errors.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: TALIS 2024 in this note relies solely on self-reports from teachers and principals (per the document), and the reported outcomes are percentages and agreement levels rather than cognitive achievement scores with plausible values. Therefore, plausible values handling is not applicable to the reported indicators in this results note. The note also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure for the underlying survey responses, so missing-data handling is treated as not reported.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note presents findings for Montenegro based on TALIS 2024 responses collected in 2024 from lower secondary teachers and principals. It does not report additional analytic restrictions (e.g., grade subsamples, exclusions, or completion thresholds) in the provided text; it only states that the note comments on statistically significant differences or changes relative to the OECD average.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD results note summarizes TALIS 2024 findings for Montenegro, focusing on lower secondary teachers and principals. The outcomes are self-reported indicators (e.g., teacher background characteristics, perceived ability to adapt teaching to diversity, special education needs context, social and emotional learning confidence, technology use including AI, opportunities to learn, induction/mentoring, professional learning needs and barriers, teacher leadership/autonomy, professional relationships, status of the profession, employment terms, sources of stress, and well-being/satisfaction/retention intentions). The note reports percentages and highlights statistically significant differences from the OECD average, but it does not present any student-level predictive modeling, plausible values, or explicit missing-data handling. As a result, the document is best interpreted as descriptive cross-sectional survey evidence for policy discussion rather than as an ML-based causal or predictive study.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive results note from the OECD TALIS 2024 database rather than an empirical ML paper. Consequently, there is no reported ML model, no target-variable prediction task, and no plausible-values framework; the note also does not provide microdata sample sizes or per-country analytic Ns in the provided text. The extraction therefore leaves total_students and per-country Ns null because the note does not report them, while still capturing the substantive survey indicators and their comparisons to the OECD average.
